Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.

Sri Sanjay Kumar Singh Advocate holding brief of Sri Anish submitted that Sri Anish has filed his power on behalf of the informant in the office of this Court but his name could not be shown in the cause list.
However, he is ready to argue the case.

2. Heard Sri Mohd. Farooq, learned counsel for the applicants; Sri Sanjay Kumar Singh Advocate holding brief of Sri Anish, learned counsel for the informant and Sri Ravi Kant Kushwaha, learned AGA for the State-respondent.
3. The instant application has been filed seeking release of the applicants on bail in Case Crime No.
49 of 2023, under Sections 304-B, 498A IPC and section 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station Karanda,
District Ghazipur, during pendency of the trial in the court below.
4. FIR of the present case was lodged against the applicants and others including their son i.e.
husband of the deceased and according to the FIR, marriage of the son of the applicants was performed with the deceased on 31.5.2022 and applicants and their family members tortured the Imarati Devi And Another vs State Of U.P. on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83750670/
1 deceased for want of dowry and on 20.4.2023 they have committed her murder.
5. Learned counsel for the applicants submitted that applicants are in-laws of the deceased and entire allegation of torture and demand of dowry made against the applicants are totally false and baseless and it appears that some dispute arose between husband and wife and due to the dispute with her husband, deceased committed suicide.

entities.text: Imarati Devi And Another vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 6. He further submitted that applicants are not having any criminal history and they are in jail in the present matter since 22.4.2023.

7. Per contra, learned AGA as well as learned counsel for the informant opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that applicants are in-laws of the deceased and their daughter-in-law died within a year from the date of her marriage in her matrimonial home under abnormal circumstances and there is also allegation of demand of dowry but they could not dispute the fact that there is no specific allegation against the applicants and as per the post mortem report of the deceased, she died due to hanging.
8.
I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

9. Applicants are in-laws of the deceased and there is no specific allegation against them and post mortem report of the deceased suggests that she died due to hanging, therefore, in my view,
applicants are entitled to be released on bail.
10. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

11. Let the applicants, namely, Imarati Devi and Gama Yadav, be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicants shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless their personal presence is exempted.
(ii) The applicants shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade them from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicants shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
12. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicants.
